alternatives_rejected.why: Own span self-time is unchanged (p50 0.01->0.01ms, 0.89x in E2), so handlers are not slowed. No CPU metric appears among its significant deviations in E3.
Memory rose about 50% (z=10 in E3), which is tiny next to the latency-90 deviation of z=16885. Self-time is also flat (E2), so the extra latency is in transit, not in processing.
Its latency deviation (z=13770 in E1) is smaller than productcatalogservice's (z=16885). It calls productcatalogservice, so its latency fits a downstream victim of the delayed inbound calls (E2).
The frontend error spike (E1) follows from upstream calls slowing down. Productcatalogservice's inbound latency rose 97.7x (E2) and its workload fell 79% (E3), consistent with callers timing out.

proposed_fix.description: Remove the injected network delay (for example, a tc/netem qdisc or a chaos rule) on productcatalogservice's network interface or inbound path. Then verify that inbound p50 latency returns to about 2ms and that frontend errors clear.
